newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa sells radio-isotope stake to U.K firm.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa sells radio-isotope stake to U.K firm.

text.p: The cabinet on Wednesday approved the sale of a 30 percent share in South Africa's nuclear medicines group AEC-Amersham (Pty) Ltd to Britain's Amersham International Plc, officials said.
Cabinet secretary Jakes Gerwel announced the deal in a statement, saying Amersham had agreed to reserve a portion of its stake for a black empowerment programme.
Lawrence Hyslop, executive general manager of the state-owned Atomic Energy Corporation (AEC), said in an interview the decision ratified an agreement with Amersham in June.

He said the sale at about one million rand ($213,220) would give AEC access to foreign markets and Amersham access to its research reactor and its underutilised hot cell complex at Pelindaba in the northeast of the country.
"There will be a two-way technology transfer, but I suppose it's fair to say more will be coming our way than going theirs," he said.
Both groups manufacture and market radio-isotope products used in high technology medicine.

Hyslop said Amersham approached the AEC earlier this year with a proposal that they work together. AEC-Amersham was formed in June as a wholly-owned subsidiary of the AEC in anticipation of a formal cooperative agreement.
"There was not very much money involved, so we had expected approval sooner. We didn't think it would have to go to the cabinet," he said.
